primary.compare.discovery: Comparing numbers means deciding which quantity is greater. Compare the number of digits first, then read positions from left to right; {1} also shows how numbers are ordered.
primary.largeNumbers.discovery: A large number is organized into ones, tens, hundreds, and thousands. A digit's position determines its value: in 24,305, the 2 represents 20,000.
primary.rounding.discovery: Rounding replaces a number with a nearby simpler value. To round to tens, inspect the ones digit: 0–4 rounds down and 5–9 rounds up.
primary.fractions.discovery: A fraction describes equal parts of a whole. The denominator tells how many equal parts there are, and the numerator tells how many are selected.
primary.multiplication.discovery: Multiplication adds the same quantity several times. In {1}, three groups of four objects make twelve objects.
primary.division.discovery: Division shares a quantity into equal groups or finds how many groups can be made. It reverses multiplication.
primary.tables.discovery: A multiplication table collects products of one number. Each result can first be rebuilt by repeatedly adding the same quantity.
primary.writtenAddition.discovery: Written addition aligns ones, tens, and hundreds. Add from the right and carry to the next column whenever a column reaches ten.
primary.writtenSubtraction.discovery: Written subtraction aligns matching positions. When a column lacks units, exchange one unit from the next column for ten.
primary.writtenMultiplication.discovery: Written multiplication splits a factor into place values. Each partial product is positioned correctly before the rows are added.
primary.writtenDivision.discovery: Written division distributes the dividend step by step. At each stage, determine how many times the divisor fits and calculate the remainder.
primary.mentalCalculation.discovery: Mental calculation turns a calculation into simple steps, such as completing a ten, splitting a number, or reusing a known result.
primary.repeatedMultiplication.discovery: Repeated multiplication uses the same factor several times. In {1}, 3 is used three times; this structure prepares power notation.
primary.lengthMeasurement.discovery: Measuring length compares a distance with a chosen unit. On a ruler, length is the difference between the ending and starting marks.
primary.lengthConversion.discovery: Converting length changes the unit without changing the distance. Each metric-table step multiplies or divides the value by 10.
primary.massMeasurement.discovery: Mass measures how much matter an object contains. A scale compares it with units such as grams and kilograms.
primary.massConversion.discovery: Mass units follow the metric table. Moving one column multiplies or divides by 10 without changing the actual mass.
primary.timeMeasurement.discovery: Duration is the time elapsed between two moments. Unlike metric units, one hour contains 60 minutes and one minute contains 60 seconds.
primary.timeCalculation.discovery: To calculate durations, combine hours and minutes separately, then exchange 60 minutes for one hour when needed.
primary.areaMeasurement.discovery: Area measures the surface covered by a shape. It is counted in unit squares; an L by W rectangle contains L × W squares.
primary.proportionality.discovery: Two quantities are proportional when the same multiplier always changes one into the other. That multiplier is the proportionality factor.
primary.pointsLines.discovery: A point marks a position, a line extends forever in both directions, and a segment is limited by two endpoints.
primary.parallelLines.discovery: Parallel lines never meet. Perpendicular lines meet to form four right angles.
primary.angles.discovery: An angle measures the opening between two rays sharing an endpoint. A right angle is 90° and a straight angle is 180°.
primary.angleMeasurement.discovery: A protractor measures an angle in degrees. Place its center on the vertex and its zero line along one side.
primary.triangles.discovery: A triangle is a polygon with three sides, three vertices, and three angles. Side lengths and angles identify its family.
primary.quadrilaterals.discovery: A quadrilateral has four sides. Parallel sides, right angles, and equal lengths distinguish squares, rectangles, rhombuses, and trapezoids.
primary.polygons.discovery: A polygon is a closed plane shape made only of segments. Its name often depends on its number of sides.
primary.circle.discovery: A circle contains all points at the same distance from its center. A radius joins the center to the circle, and a diameter equals two radii.
primary.perimeter.discovery: Perimeter is the total length around a shape. Add the lengths of every side.
primary.rectangleArea.discovery: A rectangle's area counts the unit squares covering it. It equals length multiplied by width.
primary.symmetry.discovery: An axis of symmetry divides a shape into halves that overlap when folded. Each point and its image are equally distant from the axis.
primary.solids.discovery: A solid occupies space and is described by faces, edges, and vertices. A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges, and 8 vertices.
primary.nets.discovery: A net is a plane shape that folds into a solid. A cube net uses exactly six correctly connected squares.
primary.cuboidVolume.discovery: Volume measures space in unit cubes. A cuboid contains length × width × height cubes.
primary.dataTable.discovery: A data table organizes values into rows and columns. Headings explain each value so they can be compared or totaled.
primary.chart.discovery: A chart turns data into visual shapes. A bar's height represents a value read using the axis scale.

measure.table.title: Metric unit table
measure.table.intro: Each column represents one unit. Moving to a smaller unit multiplies; moving to a larger unit divides.
measure.table.linearRule: Lengths, masses, and liters: one column means ×10 or ÷10.
measure.table.areaExplanation: The square affects two dimensions: 1 m = 10 dm, so 1 m² represents 10 dm × 10 dm.
